raw_response:
I’m old now, so I don’t want to make big changes. On my 5 mu, I’ll still do wheat followed by maize, same as before. This land suits that rotation, and if one season is a little weak, the other can still help the family. I only finished primary school, so I don’t count everything too finely. I mostly go by what worked on my own land and what the neighbors are doing. For wheat, I’ll sow in early October with a common local improved variety, not the most expensive seed. I’ll put some fertilizer before sowing, then watch the crop color after winter and add more if it looks weak. Since I have well water, I’ll irrigate a few times, but not too many because pumping costs money. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll plant maize right away. The time is tight, so I won’t do fancy tillage, just quick field prep and sowing. For maize I’ll still use hybrid seed because it gives steadier yield. I’ll use a moderate amount of fertilizer, enough to avoid losing yield, but not so much that I spend all my cash. If pests show up, I’ll spray, otherwise I won’t waste money.
